milestone: An Experience can now hold up to 5 combined content parts -- any mix of Text/Image/Graphics/Colour, repeats of the same kind allowed -- instead of exactly one
slice: Implements the user's own governing request across all 6 phases in one continuous effort: "ok lets try to incorporate multiple assets in single experience. lets allow combinations with max number of assets in an experience not exceeding 5." A follow-up confirmed repeats of the same kind (two Image parts, two Text parts, etc.) are genuinely allowed, any mix, up to 5 total, scoped to World Builder v2 only -- never v1 or root Studio. Two Explore-agent investigations plus a Plan-agent design (all independently re-verified against the live code before finalizing) confirmed the load-bearing finding: the compile pipeline (builder.js), the paint engine (engineRuntime.js), and root Studio's entire Reader-facing render/selection stack are ALL already fully N-parts-capable with zero code changes needed, since none of them have any concept of "which Experience owns this Layer" at all -- confirmed via grep that builder.js never even copies Experience-grouping info into a compiled Layer Pack entry. The entire feature is contained in the Engine Adapter (projectModel.js's _syncUniversalContent and neighbors) plus the authoring UI (worldBuilderApp.js). Phase 1 (Data model + migration + Collection dual-write foundation): experience.properties.parts holds up to 5 {id,kind,props} entries, reusing the exact existing flat field names (imageX, textContent, etc.) nested one level in -- no kind-agnostic renaming scheme, so _contentTransformFields and every existing per-field helper needed zero internal changes. A live legacy mirror keeps the top-level flat fields (imageSrc, contentKind, etc.) permanently synced to parts[0] ("the primary part") -- the deliberate, disclosed mitigation for the real fact that tools/world-builder/ (v1) and tools/world-builder-v2/ share the literal same localStorage key ('vihu-world-builder-projects'): a Project authored in v2 with multiple parts stays fully correct and editable in v1 for its own first part, with parts[1..4] simply invisible (never corrupted or lost) to v1's own UI. Phase 2 (Engine Adapter generalization): _findMirroredLayer's identity moved from a fixed kind ('slot') to a real part.id, so two same-kind parts (e.g. two Image parts) mirror onto two genuinely distinct Scene Layers instead of colliding; an orphan sweep deletes a mirrored Layer whose part was removed; same-kind parts get disambiguated Layer names ('Image', 'Image 2') so builder.js's compiled label and Object Strip cards never read identically for two different parts. Phase 3 (Collection registry fix): collectionAssetUsageCount/deleteCollectionAsset now scan parts[] instead of the derived top-level fields, so Collection's usage-count/delete-nulls-every-reference guarantee (AV-012) stays correct once an asset can live inside any of up to 5 parts on one Experience, not just one. Phase 4 (UI redesign): _renderExperienceProperties became a real part-list renderer -- each part gets its own bordered card with a disambiguated title, a Remove button, and the identical field UI the single-content-kind model always had; "+ Add a Part" (renamed from the old exclusive content-kind selector) always APPENDS a new part rather than swapping the active one; the cap is enforced at the model layer first (addExperiencePart refuses at 5, matching this codebase's established 'model-layer cap enforcement, not just a disabled UI button' discipline for e.g. Experience Graduation), with a disclosed inline message once reached. Phase 5 (Isolated Experience Studio generalization): the Stage becomes the union bounding box of every populated part's own footprint (byte-identical to before whenever exactly 1 part exists); _experienceStudioHit's hit-testing walks sections in REVERSED array order (topmost-drawn-first, since array order is paint order) instead of a fixed kind-name priority list, so two overlapping same-kind parts now correctly resolve to whichever one actually paints on top; drag/resize state moved from .slot to .partId, writing through the new part-aware updateExperiencePartProperty instead of the old single-target updateExperienceProperty. Explicitly out of scope for this feature, disclosed rather than silently omitted: reordering parts (array-append-order only, matching the precedent already set by Collection itself shipping 'add new' well before 'reorder'); changing an existing part's kind post-creation (remove + re-add instead); Place-hosted multi-part rendering (Place hosting stays Frame-only, an existing, unrelated, already-disclosed gap). Verified via 5 new/updated Playwright suites across all 6 phases -- Phase 1 (Collection dual-write + a Museum-Gallery-sourced Project migrating to a correct single-entry parts array), Phase 2 (20 assertions: same-kind mirroring, orphan sweep, name disambiguation, a real pre-existing mirrored Layer claimed in place with zero duplication on first re-sync), Phase 3 (11 assertions: usage count correctly reports 2 for two parts sharing one Collection ref, delete nulls both), Phase 4 (33 assertions: 5 mixed/repeated parts authored through the real UI, the 6th genuinely refused at the model layer even bypassing the disabled button, Remove disabled at exactly 1 part, every part's own fields surviving a real page reload with zero cross-contamination), and a new Phase 5 suite (20 assertions, built around monkey-patching the real, already-window-exposed EngineV2Runtime.rectFor/.textFootprint to record real render-call geometry rather than replicating internal coordinate math -- two spatially-separated Image parts drag independently with zero cross-target interference; two FULLY OVERLAPPING Image parts correctly move the topmost/later-added one on both a move gesture and a resize-handle gesture, proving the reversed-paint-order hit-test rather than merely 'some part moved'; a single-part Experience -- the pre-Phase-5 shape every existing theme still has -- renders exactly one section and still drags correctly through the exact same generalized code path). Full regression across the complete existing suite (goldenBuild.js for both World Builder v1 and v2; every Collection Phase 1-6 suite; every rotation suite -- image, text, text-rotation-pivot, rotation-honoured-through-real-Publish-export; the real, on-disk Museum Gallery .vtheme byte-for-byte pixel-hash regression plus its own Caption drag/resize suites; scene_dropdown_repro3.js) all pass completely unchanged. git diff confirms root Studio (js/, renderer/) and tools/world-builder/ (v1) are byte-identical/untouched throughout every phase -- this feature is confined entirely to tools/world-builder-v2/.
